verdict.rationale: A is the more faithful mechanical refactor, preserving pricing evaluation order and the exact reservation list used for rollback. B adds substantially better characterization tests and a readable top-level workflow, but changes execution order and rollback bookkeeping despite the explicit requirement that production behavior remain unchanged. Those preservation risks outweigh B's stronger test coverage.
a_issues: Adds no characterization tests, leaving important pricing boundaries, partial rollback, and notification failures unprotected.
Uses bare list annotations for reserved items rather than list[Item], and the six-argument _charge helper is somewhat cumbersome.
b_issues: Moves tax calculation and tax_rate lookup after coupon validation, whereas the original performs them first. This changes observable evaluation order and can change which exception escapes when both operations would fail.
Recomputes line prices in a second traversal instead of preserving the original combined subtotal-and-tax calculation.

Discards the successful-reservation list and releases the current order.items on payment decline. If a collaborator changes the item list during checkout, rollback can release different items than the original implementation would.
The report's blanket claim that side-effect order is unchanged overlooks the reordered pricing operations and altered rollback source.

verdict.rationale: B is the more faithful extraction, preserving the original pricing evaluation order and the recorded reservation list used for payment-failure rollback. A adds valuable characterization tests, but it moves tax calculation after coupon lookup and substitutes the current order items for the reservation snapshot, introducing avoidable behavioral differences. For a production refactor explicitly requiring unchanged behavior, B's fidelity outweighs its weaker test coverage.
a_issues: Tax calculation and tax-rate lookup now occur after coupon validation rather than before it. This changes exception precedence when tax calculation would fail and allows coupon lookup side effects to occur first.

Payment-decline cleanup uses order.items instead of the recorded successful reservations. If a collaborator changes the order's item list during checkout, rollback can release different items than the original implementation.
The report overstates preservation of execution order; the added tests do not cover the pricing-order and reservation-snapshot differences.
b_issues: Adds no characterization tests despite limited existing coverage of pricing boundaries, partial rollback, and notification failures.
Uses unparameterized list annotations for reservations; list[Item] would make the helper contracts clearer.
